summary: Stream cutoffs and 504s after dynamic system-prompt expansion in long-context calls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 504s and abrupt streaming termination when using a dynamically expanded system prompt combined with large max_tokens (>= 100k token budget). The calls initially stream tokens for several minutes then the connection abruptly ends with HTTP 504 or the finalization step fails with a timeout.

Impact:
- Affected DocuBridge production workload: document generation pipeline stalls and fails to produce final output for ~12% of requests during peak windows.
- Customer-visible 504s and truncated results that require manual retry.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: dc-dedicated-42 (prod-us-west)
- Customer namespace: docubridge-prod
- SDK: ruby-client v1.8.2 calling /v1/stream with `max_tokens` ~120000 and a system prompt that expands user history programmatically (prefix gets ~300k tokens before generation).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Assemble system prompt by concatenating user history (300k tokens) + task instructions.
2) Call streaming endpoint with max_tokens=120000, model=redwood-v2-large, streaming=true.
3) Observe streaming for ~2-5 minutes, then client sees final chunk never arrives and connection returns 504 or hangs until client timeout.

Logs / Observations:
- Ingress gateway shows long-lived upstream connections with spikes in request latency prior to 504.
- Serving runtime logs show repeated KV eviction / recompute cycles on the request's KV cache just before finalization.
- Finalizer worker reports "finalization deadline exceeded" in several traces.
- No obvious OOMs on GPUs; memory usage oscillates but stays under alloc limits.

Customer request:
DocuBridge requests an explanation and a short-term mitigation they can apply immediately (they prefer not to drop to smaller token budgets if avoidable).
comments: 2026-03-11 09:22 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and runtime team. Asked customer for exact request IDs and sample payload. SLA: P1, first response within 1 business hour.
2026-03-11 10:05 - SRE (Thomas Nguyen): Collected trace ids: trace-20260311-7f3a and trace-20260311-7f9b. Noticed repeated full KV cache flushes at token ~65k and another at ~110k for same request.

2026-03-11 11:12 - Runtime Eng (Priya Desai): Observed pattern where large prefix causes multiple kernel context switches and re-serialization of KV shards; candidate hypothesis: continuous caching eviction thrashes finalizer progress under heavy prefix expansion. Adding instrumentation to measure KV hit rate per request.

2026-03-12 08:34 - Customer (DocuBridge - Samir Rao): Provided three request payloads and allowed Redwood to run diagnostics in their dedicated cluster. They reported incidence rate spikes during batch uploads between 02:00-05:00 UTC.

2026-03-13 14:50 - SRE (Thomas Nguyen): Applied temporary routing tweak to send long-context calls to low-concurrency nodes and increased finalizer timeout to 300s for docubridge-prod. Customer reports a reduction in 504s from 12% to ~3% during a short verification run.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Following up with next steps and asking runtime eng for longer-term fix ETA.
investigation_notes: KV eviction observed: for several traces we see full KV shard evictions at ~65k and again at ~110k tokens — indicates working-set exceeded slot reservation leading to recompute of large prefixes.
Finalizer worker timeouts occur after multiple small recompute windows; finalizer backlog correlates with node concurrency and high prefix size.
No GPU OOMs; CPU-side serialization spikes increase finalization latency — likely from repeated kv-serialize + network chunking.

Hypothesis: automated prefix expansion pattern (customer-side) produces many small updates to the request prefix during generation path that disable effective prefix/KV caching; runtime ends up recomputing large parts multiple times.
We reproduced a similar pattern in staging with synthetic prefix growth and observed the same finalizer deadline exceed behavior when max_tokens > 80k and dynamic prefix updates present.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Route customer long-context traffic to a dedicated low-concurrency pool (done). 2) Increased finalizer timeout for docubridge-prod to 300s (done). 3) Recommended immediate customer mitigation: collapse history client-side (summarize) or reduce max_tokens below 40k until fix rolled out.
next_steps:
- Runtime team to implement KV eviction hysteresis: prevent full-shard eviction for requests flagged as long-context (owner: Priya Desai, ETA 2026-03-21).
- Add instrumentation to report per-request KV churn metric and alert when churn > threshold (owner: Observability team, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Postmortem & runbook update: add guidance for routing long-context interactive workloads to low-concurrency pools.
- Follow up with customer on 2026-03-16 to validate and schedule a controlled rollout of KV hysteresis fix.
resolution_notes: Workaround in place (routing + timeout bump). Permanent fix in progress: KV eviction hysteresis to reduce recompute thrashing. Will update ticket when PR lands and after controlled rollout.
estimated_impact: ~12% request failure rate at peak before mitigations; reduced to ~3% during verification after routing and timeout increases.
customer_communication_summary: Notified customer of temporary mitigation and recommended client-side summarization as short-term measure; customer accepted and requested follow-up status updates and a post-fix verification window.
